title: Graphing y = |x+1| - 2 by Transformations
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Build the graph of y=|x+1|-2 from the V-shaped graph of y=|x|, locating its vertex and intercepts.

steps.title: Start with the Parent V
steps.explanation: The absolute-value graph is a V with its apex at the origin, slope 1 on the right branch and -1 on the left.
steps.why: Piecewise: |x| = x for x >= 0 and -x for x < 0.

steps.title: Apply the Inner Shift
steps.explanation: Replacing x by x+1 slides the V one unit to the left, because x+1=0 at x=-1.
steps.why: Horizontal translations act opposite to the inner sign.

steps.title: Apply the Outer Shift
steps.explanation: Subtracting 2 outside the absolute value lowers every height by 2, moving the apex to (-1,-2).
steps.why: Vertical translations act in the direction of the sign.

steps.title: Sketch and Check Intercepts
steps.explanation: Draw the V with apex (-1,-2) and slopes -1 and +1: setting |x+1|-2=0 gives x=1 or x=-3 on the axis, and x=0 gives y=-1.
steps.why: Solving |x+1|=2 confirms the two x-intercepts, and direct substitution gives the y-intercept |0+1|-2=-1.
